title: Hammond the radical and his family wealth
summary: Hammond pushed to desegregate everything, escaped the red scare, and used his family money to pay for sessions.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And of course Mr. Hammond talked about, he was such a radical, especially about desegregating everything, not just music, night clubs, the Army when he got chose for the troops. He wanted to desegregate everything. And did. And so he was labeled a radical. And because of the “New Masses” thing, he’s a communist, but he didn’t get caught in the red scare thing in the 50s.
Yes. So he had the sort of financial luxury of taking these causes and really getting behind them.
As he said, “I had the means to pay for my” — he paid for the sessions for Basie and Billie Holiday. He paid for those things himself. He was his own bank for that stuff.
